Which of the statements is/are correct?

An enquiry into the conduct of a registered firm supplying stores is in progress, and, pending its completion, dealings with the firm are held up as a temporary step. Such suspension of business dealings with a firm, as distinct from banning it, is:

options.A: A permanent measure taken only after a full enquiry is completed
options.B: An interim measure adopted pending completion of the enquiry into the conduct of the firm
options.C: A measure applicable only to foreign firms
options.D: A measure which can be taken only after the firm has first been banned

q: Before an order banning business dealings with a firm for supply of stores is issued against it, the firm is ordinarily:

options.A: Given an opportunity to show cause and explain its position
options.B: Required to deposit the full value of all its pending orders in cash
options.C: Struck off the list of registered firms without any notice to it
options.D: Debarred automatically from tenders for one year, without any order

q: A purchase order for stores prescribes pre-despatch inspection, and the inspection is to be carried out by an agency acting on behalf of the Railways. Such inspection of purchased stores, where so prescribed, may be carried out by:

options.A: The Accounts stock verifiers of the railway
options.B: The supplier's own staff, without any independent check
options.C: RITES, acting as an inspection agency

In a railway stores depot, the book balance of every item is maintained continuously in the priced records as receipts and issues take place, and these balances are physically verified in rotation during the year. This system of inventory followed for railway stores accounts is the:

options.A: Periodic inventory system, under which stock is counted only at the end of the year
options.B: Bin card system, under which no priced records are maintained
options.C: Annual stock-taking system, dispensing with priced ledgers

q: A work returns a quantity of serviceable stores, earlier issued to it, to the depot. On examination, the stores are found fit for re-use but their present worth is less than the price at which they were originally issued. The credit to be given to the returning work for these stores is at:

options.A: The value assessed for the returned material
options.B: The price at which the stores were originally issued, in all cases
options.C: The current market price of new material of the same description
options.D: Nil, as no credit is given for stores returned to a depot

q:
Consider the following statements about a loss of stores noticed in a depot:
1. The loss can be written off straightaway by the storekeeper, without any enquiry, as soon as it is noticed.
2. Before the loss is written off, the responsibility for it is investigated and fixed, and recovery is made from the official at fault where negligence is established.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
The programme of stock verification in a stores depot is so drawn up by the Accounts Department that:

options.A: Every item held in the depot is physically verified at least once in a year
options.B: All the items of the depot are verified on one single day of the year
options.C: Only items costing above Rs 1 lakh are verified during the year
options.D: Each item is verified once in five years

q: A consignment received at a depot is opened in the presence of the carrier's representative and a part of the material is found short and another part damaged in transit. The correct course for the depot in such a case is to:

options.A: Accept the consignment silently and ignore the shortage and damage
options.B: Recover the value personally from the storekeeper, without any record
options.C: Record the shortage/damage on the receipt documents and prefer a claim on the supplier or the carrier, as the case may be
options.D: Deduct the amount from the next bill of the firm, without any record

q: Material despatched by a supplier has reached a depot and is lying there, but its inspection has not yet been completed and no receipt note has been issued for it. In the priced stock accounts of the depot, this material is taken into stock:

options.A: Immediately on its arrival at the depot gate
options.B: As soon as it is issued to a consuming department
options.C: At the end of the financial year, with the annual stock-taking
options.D: Only after it has been inspected and accepted and a receipt note issued

q: One depot of a railway despatches stores to another depot under a transfer order. Until the receiving depot acknowledges the receipt of the material, the stores so despatched remain accounted for:

options.A: In the books of the receiving depot, from the date of despatch
options.B: In no depot's books, the accounts being closed on despatch
options.C: In the books of the despatching depot
options.D: In the personal account of the storekeeper of the receiving depot

q: Under the periodic review (periodic ordering) system of inventory control followed for a stock item:

options.A: Stock is reviewed at fixed intervals and an order is placed to restore the stock to a predetermined target level
options.B: A fixed quantity is ordered whenever the stock falls to the re-order level
options.C: Orders are placed only when the stock is completely exhausted
options.D: The supplier himself reviews the stock and despatches material automatically

q: Stores are purchased against a specific demand of a work, are received at the depot and are passed on to the work without being stocked as regular depot stock. Such non-stock stores are accounted for by:

options.A: Taking them into the priced stock of the depot like stock items
options.B: Crediting their value to Purchase Suspense
options.C: Including them in the closing balance of stores of the railway
options.D: Charging their cost direct to the work or department concerned, without routing them through the stock accounts

q: Against a purchase order for 1,000 units of an item, a supplier delivers 650 units, which are received, inspected and accepted at the depot; the balance quantity is still awaited. The supplier's bill for the supply made is passed for payment:

options.A: For the full quantity of 1,000 units ordered, as the order is a concluded contract
options.B: Only for the quantity of 650 units actually received and accepted
options.C: For 98 per cent of the value of the full order, in all cases
options.D: Only after the entire quantity ordered has been received at the depot

q: A firm supplies stores which do not fully conform to the specification in the purchase order, but the stores are usable for the intended purpose and the deviation is not material. Such stores may be accepted:

options.A: By the competent authority under a deviation, with a suitable reduction in price
options.B: By the depot storekeeper at the full contract price
options.C: Only if the supplier agrees to replace them during the warranty period
options.D: In no circumstances; such stores must always be rejected outright

q:
Consider the following statements about the pricing of stores issues in the priced accounts:
1. Each issue is valued at the purchase rate of the oldest lot held in stock, following the first-in-first-out method.
2. Issues are valued at the prevailing (average) book rate of the item, irrespective of the lot from which the material is physically drawn.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

Consider the following statements about the pricing of stores moving out of a depot:
1. Stores transferred from one depot to another depot of the same railway are priced at the book rate, without addition of departmental charges.
2. Stores issued to outside parties and other Government departments are priced at the book rate plus the prescribed departmental charges.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.B: GeM is used by the Railways only for the sale of scrap
options.C: IREPS is the national marketplace for common-use goods and services

q: For working out the cost of holding stores, a finance officer has to state how the inventory carrying cost of a railway is ordinarily expressed. It is ordinarily expressed as:

options.A: A-category items are consumed only once in many years
options.B: A-category items are never required in an emergency
options.C: A large amount of capital is locked up in every unit of A-category stock, so an excess buffer is costly

q: A depot officer reporting on the stock position of an item states its 'coverage' as four months. In stores parlance, the coverage of a stock item means:

options.C: The validity period of the tender under which the item is purchased
